name: Alicante
title: Alicante Hull Gauging | Ultrasonic Thickness Measurement Ships
description: Thickness measurement at Alicante for Algeria and Balearic ferries, cruise ships, bulkers and coasters: UTM of hull, decks, tanks and scrubber piping.
h1: Ship Thickness Surveys in Alicante: Ferries, Cruise Ships and Bulk Cargo
intro: Alicante's harbour sits right in front of the city and works as a ferry port to Algeria and the Balearic Islands, a cruise stop and a smaller cargo gateway for cement, stone and general freight. Ships on fixed timetables are easy to plan around, and that suits ultrasonic gauging. We send technicians from India to the vessel, with port passes arranged by the ship's agent, and match the scope to what each ship type can offer alongside.

highlights.p: Ferries sailing to Oran, Algiers and the islands lie alongside between departures. That gap is long enough for focused readings of ramps, car decks, ballast tanks and fire main piping when access is prepared by the crew.

Cruise ships dock for a day and leave, so gauging is limited to prepared spaces. Voids, sea-water lines and tanks selected by the technical department give useful readings without disturbing guests or the sailing time.

Ships loading cement, stone or salt-related cargoes from this stretch of coast give access to holds and decks between operations. We read frames, coamings and tank tops once the hold is clear and the loading plan allows.

port.h: The port of Alicante: passenger quays beside the old town
p: The Autoridad Portuaria de Alicante manages a compact harbour in the centre of the city, framed by breakwaters that shelter a basin open to the south-east. The approach is uncomplicated and the pilots board outside the entrance, although a brisk easterly can make the entry lively and delay a ship. Passenger and ferry terminals occupy the quays closest to the seafront and the Santa Bárbara hill, while cargo berths are placed on the outer and southern sides, so the commercial and leisure uses of the harbour are kept apart.

Alicante's passenger traffic is varied. Ferries cross to the Algerian ports of Oran and Algiers, and services link the city with the Balearic Islands during the summer season. Cruise ships call throughout the year, and the port is also popular as a yacht base, which means the basin carries a lot of marina traffic as well. On the cargo side, the port ships cement, stone, aggregates and general goods, and trades in cereal and fertiliser pass through in smaller volumes. The nearby salt works at Torrevieja send out salt through their own harbour, so some bulk tonnage in this area never calls at Alicante itself.

Seasons set the rhythm. Passenger services peak in summer, and ferries run hard when returning families and holidaymakers fill the decks. Winter is the quiet period when ships schedule maintenance and surveys, often elsewhere. Tidal range is small and has little effect on berth depth, so planning is shaped by wind, berth allocation and the ship's schedule. The anchorage off the port is used by ships waiting for a berth or for cargo, and some coasters spend several days there between voyages. Good agent liaison is the key to a smooth survey, because quay space can change at short notice.

Most thickness work in Alicante is done at the berth. Ferries on the Algerian route have a few hours between arrival and departure, and between those the ramp, car deck and tank tops are accessible once the vehicles are gone. Cruise ships have their turnaround time, and the technical department can have selected spaces ventilated and tested. Cargo ships at the outer quays give longer stays and easier access to holds, decks and hatch covers, as long as the terminal agrees and the cargo plan leaves space clear.

There is no drydock for ocean-going ships in the harbour. Small craft, tugs and yachts are handled by local boatyards, but merchant ships needing steel renewal usually dock at Cartagena, Valencia or a yard further afield. This makes Alicante a good place to prepare the docking: readings taken here give the superintendent a measured scope to take to the yard, and the technicians can continue the work at the docking port if required. Anchorage jobs are possible for short sampling work when a launch and calm water are available.
list: Ferry berths for Algeria and the islands — ramp, car-deck, ballast tank and fire main gauging between departures
Cruise quays — voids, sea-water cooling lines and scrubber piping on turnaround days, as prepared by the technical department
Outer cargo quays — hold frame, hatch coaming and deck readings on bulk carriers and general cargo ships
Boatyards for tugs and small craft — hull plating readings before a haul-out or repair
Alicante anchorage — short sampling jobs on coasters and bulkers waiting for a berth or orders
Docking yards at Cartagena and Valencia — gauging started here continues alongside the docking survey

context.h: Port state control and shipping context for Alicante
p: Port state control is exercised in Alicante under the Paris MoU by the Capitanía Marítima, part of Spain's Dirección General de la Marina Mercante. Ferries on international routes to Algeria receive attention to structure, watertight integrity and fire safety, and corrosion of ballast tanks and piping can be recorded as a deficiency if a master cannot show measurements. Cruise ships and cargo vessels face the same checks, and recent thickness readings are a practical response when an inspector asks about condition.

EU measures add context for owners operating from Spanish waters. Ships calling at EU ports need an Inventory of Hazardous Materials under the Ship Recycling Regulation, and EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime shape decisions on energy and retrofits for ferry and cruise operators. The Algerian service is run with fairly mature tonnage, and operators look at how much steel will need to be renewed before committing to another season. Where a retrofit exposes structure that is normally closed up, taking readings at that moment can prevent a repeat visit to the same space later.

jobs.p: Work at Alicante usually fits one of three patterns: programmed visits to ferries on set rotations, short calls on cruise ships, and longer work on cargo ships with time alongside. Scope, access and report layout are agreed with the superintendent before the technicians travel, so the hours at the quay are spent measuring. Examples that suit this port:
list: Car-deck, ramp and ballast tank gauging on an Algeria route ferry during a winter lay-over.
Sea-water line, void and scrubber piping readings on a cruise ship on a turnaround day.
Hold frame and hatch coaming gauging on a bulk carrier after discharge at the outer quay.
Pre-docking steel estimate on a coaster or ferry, with readings taken in Alicante before the yard in Cartagena or Valencia is selected.
Condition gauging on a ship being sold or chartered, giving the buyer measured hull and tank data.

logistics: Alicante-Elche Airport is a short road journey from the port and has wide European connections, plus routes through Gulf and other hubs that suit travel from India. The ship's agent arranges port passes for the ferry and cargo areas and a launch for any anchorage work. Schengen visas are required for the technicians, so send the vessel's dates as early as you can; once visas are issued we confirm mobilisation against the ship's timetable.

faqs.q: Can an Algeria ferry be gauged between departures?
faqs.a: Often, yes. With ramps down and car decks empty, plating, ballast tanks and piping can be gauged if the crew prepares access. The time between arrival and sailing is limited, so a targeted list works best; deeper programmes involving gas-freeing or staging are better placed in the ship's overhaul period.

faqs.q: Is there a drydock at Alicante?
faqs.a: Not for merchant ships of any size. Small craft and yachts use boatyards, while ferries and cargo ships needing renewal normally dock in Cartagena, Valencia or further afield. Gauging in Alicante gives the owner a measured steel estimate before a yard is chosen, and helps compare quotations.

faqs.q: What can be done during a cruise call?
faqs.a: Short readings in voids, sea-water piping, scrubber lines and selected tanks, provided the technical department prepares the spaces and entry permits in advance. Anything needing staging, cleaning or long gas-freeing should wait for a dry-dock period. We agree the list with the hotel and technical teams before the ship arrives.

faqs.q: Can ships at the Alicante anchorage be surveyed?
faqs.a: Short jobs are possible, depending on launch access, swell and the agent's clearance. A coaster or bulker waiting for cargo can give time, but it may move at short notice. We prefer a narrow, well-defined scope at anchor and leave larger programmes for a berth stop.

faqs.q: Are bulk carrier holds accessible at the outer quays?
faqs.a: After discharge and cleaning, yes, if the loading plan leaves the hold empty and the terminal permits entry. We read frames, hopper and bulkhead plating and hatch coamings, and stop when cargo operations resume. The hold order is agreed with the chief officer beforehand.
